title: Kitesurfing La Ventana
coverImageAlt: Placeholder — real kitesurfing photo to come
excerpt: By January the wind lines in La Ventana are steady enough to set a watch by.
subtitle: The wind that ruins a sailing afternoon in La Paz is the same wind that makes La Ventana one of the more reliable kite spots in Baja.
author: Thibault Poirson
body:
La Ventana sits about an hour from La Paz, on the other side of the peninsula from the calm water we usually sail. The same north wind that keeps the bay flat pushes hard through the channel there, thermal and mechanical effects stacking on top of each other most winter afternoons.

We'll sometimes swap a sailing day for a kite day when the forecast lines up, trading the catamaran for boards and letting the crew who kite teach the rest of us badly for an afternoon.

> It's the same wind. It just does something completely different depending on which side of the peninsula you're standing on.

![Placeholder — real photo of the beach at La Ventana to come](/assets/img/hero-premium.webp "The beach at La Ventana, mid-afternoon, well before the wind picks up.")

Most of us are bad at it, which is part of why it's a good afternoon off. Nobody on the boat is trying to be good at kitesurfing.

By the time the sun starts to drop the wind usually eases, and we head back to La Paz with sand in everything and no particular urgency about it.
